$comment: Product backlog for the agile board. scripts/bootstrap-board.mjs turns each story into a GitHub issue on the project board. Keep in sync with the Milestone 2 doc.

milestones.title: M2 · Walking skeleton
milestones.description: One feature end to end through the real architecture.

milestones.title: MVP
milestones.description: Sign-in, groups, all split types, balances, settle-up, confirmations.

milestones.title: Stretch
milestones.description: Recurring bills and the AI fairness summary (cut first).

stories.title: Sign in and keep my data across devices
stories.story: As Josh, I want to sign in with Google or my school email so that my balances follow me to any phone and nobody else can post expenses as me.
criteria: Given a new user, when Josh signs in with Google or an email link, then an account is created with his display name.
Any API call without a valid token returns 401; a call on a group he is not in returns 403.
After signing in on a second phone, Josh sees the same groups and balances.

stories.title: Create a group and invite roommates
stories.story: As Maya, I want to create a group and invite my roommates with a link so that the whole house shares one ledger.
criteria: Given Maya is signed in, when she creates "Maple St House", then she is its first member and admin.
When a roommate opens the invite link while signed in, they join and see the same balances as Maya.
An invite link expires after 7 days, and the admin can revoke it sooner.

stories.title: Add an expense split evenly
stories.story: As Maya, I want to log a shared expense in a few taps and have it split evenly so that I never have to do the math or explain it.
criteria: Given a 4-person group, when Maya saves "Groceries, $50.00, paid by Maya", then each share is $12.50 and Maya's balance rises by $37.50.
Given $10.00 split 3 ways, shares are $3.34, $3.33 and $3.33: leftover cents go to members in join order, and shares always sum to the total.
The amount must be $0.01 to $10,000.00 and the description 1 to 80 characters; otherwise an inline error shows and nothing is saved.
Saving twice with the same request key (double tap or network retry) records one expense, not two.
The group screen shows the new balances right after saving, with no manual refresh.

stories.title: Split by percentage or custom amounts
stories.story: As Maya, I want to split an expense by percentages or exact amounts so that uneven costs, like a bigger bedroom's rent, are logged correctly.
criteria: Custom amounts must add up to the total; until they do, Save is disabled and the difference is shown.
Percentages must add up to 100%; leftover cents are assigned in join order, as in US-03.
A member can be left out of an expense with a share of $0.00.

stories.title: See my net balance per group
stories.story: As Josh, I want one number per group that says what I owe or am owed so that I stop scrolling through five group chats.
criteria: The group screen shows each member's net (paid minus share) as "owes $X" or "is owed $X".
The home screen shows Josh's net across all of his groups.
A group's member balances always sum to exactly $0.00.
Only expenses and confirmed settlements count; pending settlements are listed separately.

stories.title: Get the fewest payments to settle up
stories.story: As Maya, I want the app to suggest the fewest payments that clear the group so that I am not chasing five small Venmo requests.
criteria: For groups of up to 12 members, the plan uses the true minimum number of payments; larger groups get a plan with at most N-1 payments.
Making every suggested payment brings every member's balance to $0.00.
Each suggestion shows payer, receiver and an exact amount, and the plan updates after any expense or settlement change.

stories.title: Confirm a settlement on both sides
stories.story: As Maya, I want a payment to count only after both of us confirm it so that the balances stay trustworthy for the whole group.
criteria: When Josh records "Paid Maya $42.50", it shows as Pending for both of them and balances do not change yet.
Balances change only when Maya confirms; she can also reject it with a reason.
Every settlement keeps an audit record of who recorded it, who confirmed it, when, and how much.

stories.title: Get reminded about unpaid balances
stories.story: As Josh, I want a reminder when I have owed money for a while so that I pay back without Maya having to nag me.
criteria: If Josh has owed money in a group for 3 days, he gets one push reminder, and at most one per group every 3 days after that.
Josh can mute reminders for a group.
Tapping the reminder opens that group's settle-up screen.

stories.title: See my monthly shared spending
stories.story: As Priya, I want to see what I spend on shared costs each month so that I can budget ahead instead of being surprised by a utility bill.
criteria: The summary shows Priya's share per calendar month for the last 6 months, per group and in total.
The current month is broken down by category: rent, utilities, groceries and other.
Each month's total equals the exact sum of her shares for that month.

stories.title: Auto-add recurring bills
stories.story: As Priya, I want rent and WiFi to be added automatically each month so that nobody forgets and I can plan around them.
criteria: A template stores description, amount, payer, split and a day of the month from 1 to 28.
The scheduler posts the expense once on that day; running the job twice never creates a duplicate.
Members are notified when a recurring expense posts, and the template can be paused or edited.

stories.title: Get a neutral AI fairness summary
stories.story: As Maya, I want a neutral written summary of contribution patterns so that the group can talk about imbalances without me being the one to bring it up.
criteria: Any member can request a summary of the last 30 or 90 days; it appears within 10 seconds, or the app shows "Summary unavailable" with the plain numbers still visible.
Every number in the summary matches the statistics the server computed; the model is not allowed to introduce new figures.
The model receives aliases ("Member A") and totals only, never names, emails or expense descriptions.
Wording describes amounts, not motives ("paid 18% less than an even share", not "is freeloading").
